newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Property developers give HK vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Property developers give HK vote of confidence.

text.p: Property developers gave Hong Kong's real estate market an overwhelming vote of confidence on Tuesday by bidding up a plot of land for more than two hours to a record price, analysts said.
A consortium, owned equally by Sino Land Co Ltd and its chairman Robert Ng's family, bought the 25,592 square metre plot in Chai Wan for HK$11.82 billion.
Ng said the consortium would spend about HK$20 billion to develop the site on the eastern side of Hong Kong island.
Government land agent Herbert Leung said it was the highest price ever paid for a site at a Hong Kong government auction.
"It is certainly a record price," he said.

Sino Land was obviously willing to take a very aggressive approach to the market and would have to sell for at least HK$8,000 per square foot to justify the price, said David Faulkner, a partner at property consultancy Brooke Hillier Parker.
"It means they are looking at a 25 to 30 percent price increase (from current market levels)," he said.
Analysts had expected the site, earmarked for non-industrial use, to fetch anywhere between HK$6.0 billion to HK$14.8 billion.
"I think the auctioneers tried to get every penny out of the bidder," said Amsteel Securities head of research Edward Chan, noting the drawn out bidding of more than two hours.

He said if Sino Land wanted to earn a profit margin of 40 percent, it was looking at a target price of HK$10,800 to HK$11,000 per square foot upon completion of the development project, which could take about three years.
Analysts said Sino Land had been bullish on the property market for many years.
"They do have a record for paying top dollar," said Michael Clarke, professional services director at Colliers Jardine.

Steven Brown, research director at NAVA SC Securities, said Sino Land would have to pay more for a site of that size than bigger property developers because it did not have the same financial strength, reputation or land bank planning skills.
But he said although the price was "aggressive", Sino Land had been a very shrewed buyer of land over the last 10 years.
"Quite a lot of people are similarly bullish about property and confident about Hong Kong and the future of the property market," added Clarke.

Market sources said CITIC Pacific Ltd, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd and New World Development Co Ltd were among the 15 bidders for the site.
China Overseas Land and Investment Ltd bought a second plot of land of 2,627 square metres situated at Ho Man Tin in Kowloon for HK$1.4 billion.
Industry analysts had expected the residential site to fetch between HK$848 million and HK$1.27 billion.
The Hong Kong government has auctioned 10 plots of land during the 1996/97 fiscal year fetching HK$15.46 billion.
Tuesday's auction was the final auction this fiscal year ending March 31.
